public_rationale: The studies document consumer value and paid use. Neither establishes what comparable unsubsidized service would cost or how most users would respond. They therefore qualify the rhetoric without disproving subsidy dependence. The available evidence also does not connect enterprise cost complaints to verified full-cost pricing in the target period.
limitations: The consumer studies concern US users, while the claim has no geographic restriction.
Willingness to accept compensation is not willingness or ability to pay.
The paid-subscription observation is outside the target quarter and is context only.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Demand for AI services is a mirage built on subsidized subscriptions, and LLMs priced at true cost would be unaffordable for most users.

statement.excerpt: While there could be a theoretical future of LLMs run at their true cost (IE: unaffordable for most) as I covered in last week’s premium newsletter, that would require demand, and as I’ve discussed above, the demand for AI services is a mirage built on subsidized subscriptions, and companies paying the actual costs are already screaming for mercy.

from_speaker: LLMs run at their true cost
the demand for AI services is a mirage built on subsidized subscriptions
companies paying the actual costs are already screaming for mercy
our_interpretation: The core assertion is causal: subsidies sustain demand that would largely disappear at prices covering the costs of providing comparable services.
True cost includes infrastructure, inference, personnel, and a defensible allocation of model development and other shared costs.
Most means more than half of the relevant existing users, not merely a few unusually intensive users.
Unaffordable concerns users' ability to sustain payment; unwillingness to buy is related but not identical.
Screaming for mercy is read as material customer cost pressure, such as curtailed deployments or documented budget overruns.

The current-state component is anchored to January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter ordinarily reportable before the post. The price counterfactual concerns those users and services.
criteria.support_condition: Credible cost accounting and representative pricing or retention evidence show that subsidies explain most observed demand, that more than half of relevant users cannot afford comparable full-cost service, and that customers paying such prices experience material cost pressure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows substantial durable demand at verified full-cost prices and that most relevant users can afford comparable service. A profitable niche or a few satisfied customers alone would not settle the population-wide assertion.
